name: Speech-to-Text Forced Alignment Benchmark
description: The speech community has established open benchmarks for various aspects of speech processing. However, a comprehensive benchmark for time alignment of speech and corresponding transcripts, known as forced alignment, is notably absent. This paper provides a thorough study of this problem. The key contributions are: 1) An extensive evaluation and comparison of forced alignment algorithms; 2) A study of the robustness of alignment methods against channel variation and additive noise; 3) Investigation of forced alignment on long conversational telephone speech audios. 4) Exploration of forced alignment in low-resource languages. The key findings are: 1) Neural aligners demonstrate nearly equivalent accuracy as Hidden Markov Model (HMM) approaches for short utterances; 2) The Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) segmentation approach shows significant robustness; 3) Enlarging the CTC window size significantly improves the CTC alignment accuracy of long audio segments; 4) Off-the-shelf models don't generalize well to conversational telephone speech data and lower-resource languages. Forced alignment of long conversational audio and lower-resource languages remains a challenging problem.
reputation: Academic benchmark intended for systematic evaluation of forced-alignment quality; of interest to ASR and speech-tooling researchers and practitioners.
notes: Measures timestamp alignment accuracy rather than end-to-end ASR performance; results heavily dependent on transcript quality, speaker labels, and audio conditions; not an LLM benchmark.
